newsitem.title: USA: Stocks rally after previous session's plunge.
newsitem.headline: Stocks rally after previous session's plunge.

text.p: Blue chip stocks, led by a rally in shares of Philip Morris Cos Inc., rebounded on Friday, a day after falling 160 points on fears of an interest rate hike by the Federal Reserve.
The recovery was supported by a rise in the bond market, which rose after the release of surprisingly weak February U.S. economic data.

At about 10 a.m. EST (1500 GMT), the Dow Jones industrial average was up 40.41 at 6,919.30. In the broader market, advances led declining issues by about 12 to five on volume of 73 million on the New York Stock Exchange.

On Thursday, the Dow fell 160.48 points to close at 6,878.89 -- the fifth-steepest fall in point terms in the history of the index. That decline of 2.28 percent, however, ranked nowhere near the top percentage losses.
Philip Morris, among the big losers on Thursday, bounced 2-3/4 to 128-3/4, adding more than six points to the Dow.
The Nasdaq Composite index rose 7.84 points to 1,301.12.
Stocks and bonds rose on news that U.S. prices at the wholesale level tumbled in February, the latest signs that the economy continues to grow without inflationary pressures.
The Producer Price Index fell 0.4 percent after declining 0.3 percent in January. It was the first time since the autumn of 1994 that the index retreated two months in a row.
"This is a very good report and indicates that there is really no inflation to worry about at the producer level," said Marilyn Shaja, money market economist at DLJ Securities Corp.
Moreover, the government reported that inventories held by businesses edged up 0.1 percent in January as more goods remained on the shelves of manufacturers and wholesalers.

In a separate report, the Federal Reserve said industrial production climbed 0.5 percent in February after a revised 0.1 percent drop in January, the strongest monthly pickup in output since a 0.8 percent jump last November.
Analysts said the report was comforting from an inflation viewpoint.
The data eased concerns that the Fed, at its policy-making meeting on March 25, will raise interest rates to slow the economy's growth.
In the inflation-wary bond market, the 30-year Treasury up 4/32, or $1.25 on a $1,000 bond, reducing the yield to 6.95 percent from 6.96 percent at Thursday's close.
